correctness.rationale: For every prime and arbitrary three residue perturbations, exact expansion x=r+pt proves the stationary critical-root formula. For primitive frequencies the derivative-root criterion is proved using the maximum of two odd-order roots and small-prime cyclotomic/noncancellation exceptions. For imprimitive frequencies the p-th cyclotomic minimal polynomial gives a permutation criterion. Independent derivative and cubic-permutation counts yield the exact nullity; Fourier diagonalization yields the rank. A separately implemented cyclotomic histogram verifier passed exhaustive and sampled checks at p=2,3,5,7,11,13. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The cubic moment curve is a natural Fourier test object; the theorem classifies its entire prime-square Fourier nullspace in all characteristics and proves universal support rigidity over p^{2p} genuinely distinct residue-digit deformations. The exact p=2,3 boundary, prime modulo 3 correction and density-one-half asymptotics are nontrivial structural data, distinct from individual classical character-sum evaluations. It is not a claim about nonzero multipliers or higher exponents.
